record.title: AgentPProf adds semantic resource profiling across long-horizon agent runs
record.summary: A Sep. 14 arXiv paper introduces AgentPProf, which segments agent trajectories into nested semantic task intervals and folds token, time or operation counts into standard pprof profiles. In the paper's evaluations, it reaches 0.764 B³ F1 against human stage labels and improves mean average precision when combined with direct diagnostics on three problem-localization benchmarks. These are author-reported results; independent replication and broader multi-project evaluation remain open.
organizations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper proposes a semantic operation stack and recursive segmentation method that groups trajectory operations into nested task intervals, then folds additive measures into a standard pprof profile.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 405 CodeTraceBench trajectories with 2,948 human-annotated stages, the paper reports 0.764 B³ F1 for Codex-based segmentation versus 0.663 for its strongest automatic recurrence baseline; the paper reports 0.480 boundary F1 versus 0.266.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On complete released workloads from AgentProcessBench, TraceElephant and HINTBench, the paper reports that adding AgentPProf grouping to direct diagnostics increased MAP by 0.031, 0.107 and 0.117 respectively, with all three differences reported as statistically significant.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In one ToolSandbox repair case and 23 held-out confirmation scenarios, the paper reports a one-line compatibility fix that removed the observed syntax failures and reduced model-token use by 19.0% while clearing a fixed similarity threshold.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The reported evaluation is from the paper authors. The paper notes that multi-project evaluation and integration with tracing ecosystems remain future work; this review found no independent reproduction of its central performance results.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent group has reproduced the reported semantic agreement or localization MAP improvements.
Generalization across teams, agent stacks and operational environments is not established by the reviewed evaluation.
One reported repair case does not establish that profiler-guided inspection routinely improves repair quality or total task cost.

brief.importance_rationale: If its reported results hold, semantic profiling could help teams identify where long-running agents spend tokens and time and locate recurring failures, changing observability and debugging practice across agent systems; the paper's evaluations remain author-reported.
limitations: The evaluation results are claims in a single author paper and have not been independently reproduced in this review.
Human-stage agreement and benchmark localization are not equivalent to improved agent reliability in deployment.
The principal method uses an LLM segmenter; segmentation and its token cost may vary across models and instructions.
The reported evidence does not establish broad adoption, causal improvements across projects or superiority for every observability task.
organizations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
brief.summary: A Sep. 14 arXiv paper introduces AgentPProf, which segments agent trajectories into nested semantic task intervals and folds token, time or operation counts into standard pprof profiles. In the paper's evaluations, it reaches 0.764 B³ F1 against human stage labels and improves mean average precision when combined with direct diagnostics on three problem-localization benchmarks. These are author-reported results; independent replication and broader multi-project evaluation remain open.

technical.claimed_result: On 405 CodeTraceBench trajectories (2,948 human-annotated stages), the paper reports 0.764 B³ F1 and 0.480 boundary F1 for Codex segmentation, compared with 0.663 and 0.266 for the strongest automatic baseline. For direct diagnostics combined with AgentPProf on three failure-localization workloads, it reports MAP increases of 0.031, 0.107 and 0.117. A single ToolSandbox repair case reports 19.0% lower model-token use on held-out confirmation scenarios.
technical.compute_or_cost: Paper reports one-time Codex segmentation of 405 CodeTraceBench trajectories in 37 minutes using up to four workers, averaging 29,754 input and 573 output tokens per trajectory. Deterministic profile construction is reported at sub-second scale for tested datasets; segmentation dominates cost.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv record establishes the paper's existence and submission date. The linked public AgentSight repository documents an AgentPProf profile workflow and provides its implementation guide. This review did not run the tool or independently reproduce the paper's measurements.
technical.mechanism: Trajectory events such as prompts, model calls, tool invocations, file reads and process events are normalized into operations. A segmenter assigns nested semantic responsibility intervals; identical semantic paths are folded across sessions while tokens, time or operation count become profile widths. Output is a pprof protobuf readable by go tool pprof.
technical.novelty: Applies semantic responsibility intervals to agent profiling, folding semantically similar tasks across runs while retaining concrete LLM/tool operations as leaves and emitting a standard pprof format.
technical.regime: The paper evaluates 405 CodeTraceBench trajectories, 287 OSWorld-Human sessions, 1,012 AgentBoard goals, published action labels, 41 long-horizon coding-agent sessions, 440 mixed web-agent trajectories, and full released snapshots for three problem-localization benchmarks. The localization benchmark trajectories average 8–52 operations; long-horizon behavior is covered by smaller author-held session collections.
technical.reproducibility: The paper and an MIT-licensed public AgentSight repository are accessible. No independent replication was found or conducted in this review. The reported localization results depend on benchmark snapshots, judge configurations and annotation procedures described by the authors; broader external and multi-project evaluations remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: For semantic-stage agreement, the paper's strongest automatic baseline is multi-resolution statistical recurrence (B³ F1 0.663; boundary F1 0.266). For failure localization, the principal comparison is each benchmark's direct per-operation diagnostic alone versus the same diagnostic augmented with AgentPProf grouping.

brief.title: AgentPProf adds semantic resource profiling across long-horizon agent runs
brief.why_it_matters: Long agent traces are difficult to compare across runs when the same task is expressed through different tools and action sequences. AgentPProf proposes a semantic grouping layer that preserves underlying operations while making task-level costs and recurring failure locations visible in a familiar profiling format. If the reported results generalize, it could improve diagnosis and cost allocation for long-running agents.
